requirements.requirement: Inventory web application running on node2, listening on port 8080
requirements.summary: systemd unit inventory-app.service created, enabled, and active on node2; python3 listening on 0.0.0.0:8080 confirmed via ss; /inventory endpoint returns JSON with host=node2. Also confirmed post-restart (recovered and re-verified).

requirements.requirement: Inventory web application running on node3, listening on port 8080
requirements.summary: systemd unit inventory-app.service created, enabled, and active on node3; python3 listening on 0.0.0.0:8080 confirmed via ss; /inventory endpoint returns JSON with host=node3. Also confirmed post-restart.

requirements.requirement: node1 configured to load-balance incoming HTTP requests across both backends on port 80
requirements.summary: nginx installed and configured on node1 with an upstream (inventory_backend) containing node2:8080 and node3:8080, round-robin, listening on 0.0.0.0:80. nginx -t passed, service active, ss confirms port 80 listening. A 20-request sample showed an exact 10/10 split between the two backends, directly demonstrating load balancing.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct evidence: inventory-app systemd services are active on node2 and node3 on port 8080 returning correct host-identified JSON, and nginx on node1 load-balances port 80 across both backends with a verified even 10/10 traffic split. Beyond the public contract, the executor also ran the independent provider-wide restart protocol on all three nodes, each showing a pre-restart healthy baseline with boot_id, a reboot acknowledgement, an unreachable window, a distinct post-restart boot_id, and full recovery of the relevant service (nginx on node1, inventory-app on node2/node3) plus restored/rejoined load-balancing — all cross-confirmed by the fixed after-executor boot-identity and listening-socket snapshots. No unnecessary mutations or residue were identified.
limitations: The task instruction itself does not require restart/reboot durability, so restart evidence quality affects confidence/hygiene framing only, not the material outcome scoring.
Evidence is limited to captured command stdout/stderr; live inspection of the systems was not possible, so conclusions rely entirely on the provided transcript and fixed snapshots.
The base64-encoded app.py payload contents were not inspected directly (only its parse success and runtime JSON output), so the full application source was not reviewed.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all 41 executor commands chronologically. Every state-changing command (apt-get install nginx on node1; mkdir/app.py writes and systemd unit creation on node2/node3; nginx site config and enable on node1; the three sequential `reboot` invocations) maps directly to a material task outcome or to the independently-required restart protocol. No unnecessary, unbounded, or unreverted experimental mutations were found. The 4 failed commands (return_code -1) are expected connection drops/timeouts while polling nodes during their own reboots, not troubleshooting mistakes, and each is followed by a successful reconnection. Post-executor package-health and failed-services checks show clean state (manager=dpkg, no failed units) on all three nodes, and only expected ephemeral systemd-private /tmp entries and the new nginx/python3 listening sockets differ from baseline.
